newsitem.title: USA: Miami police reject wage concession plan.
newsitem.headline: Miami police reject wage concession plan.

text.p: Miami's police union rejected a wage concession package aimed at helping the city close a $68 million budget gap, city officials said Monday.
The Fraternal Order of Police voted 299-531 against the plan.

All city employees were asked to accept a two-year delay in scheduled four-percent cost-of-living raises, as well as cuts in benefits. The proposal would have saved the city $25 million over two years.

The firefighters, sanitation workers and general employee unions approved the plan. The City Commission will meet Thursday to ratify new agreements with those three unions, which would save $19 million, said Sue Weller, the city's labor relations liaison.

The city sought $6 million in concessions from police. In addition to the wage freeze, officers who take home city-owned cars were asked to pay $80 a month, and all officers were asked to accept cuts in health insurance benefits.
"The city is looking to sit down with them again to try to work out a deal that's acceptable, as long as we are within the $6 million that they need to come up with," Weller said.

Police union leaders endorsed the plan after their accountants verified the city's deficit figures for the year that began Oct 1. But the officers said they were being unfairly punished for mismanagement by city officials.
The deficit was discovered after the city manager and finance director resigned to face corruption charges.
Miami has declared a fiscal emergency, which would allow it to reopen its union contracts. Weller said that at least for now, the city would continue to seek voluntary concessions.
